All stations

Training track · 21 stations · 20 levels · 1590 lessons

Property Management — Twenty Zones

SEIU 87 and SEIU-USWW janitors and building staff, IUOE Local 39 stationary engineers, UNITE HERE for residential hospitality staff, and the apartment association's certified apartment manager and maintenance technician credentials

OSHA 29 CFR 1910 general industry, NFPA 72 and 25 for fire alarm and sprinkler systems, the state elevator code, the Fair Housing Act, the state landlord-tenant statute, the local housing code, and EPA lead and asbestos rules for pre-1978 buildings

A working building as twenty zones, each its own station: lobby to roof, boiler room to trash room, leasing office to fire panel, with the tenant, the inspector and the contractor in the scene.

20 / 20levels at 75+ lessons
1590lessons across the track
124tasks: a station under a condition
0more stations needed to fill it

Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

What it proves

Competency: Run a building zone by zone under the fire, housing and safety codes that govern it

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 6 of its 21 stations, against OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout); NFPA 25 Standard for the Inspection, Testing, and Maintenance of Water-Based Fire Protection Systems.

These stations also count toward:

  • Lockout/Tagout and the control of hazardous energy (1 of this track's stations count toward it)

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: OSHA 29 CFR 1910 general industry, NFPA 72 and 25 for fire alarm and sprinkler systems, the state elevator code, the Fair Housing Act, the state landlord-tenant statute, the local housing code, and EPA lead and asbestos rules for pre-1978 buildings. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
